parsed.explanation: A trans visitor cannot align documents with presentation, and national law expressly criminalises cross-dressing/posing as another sex, with at least one documented prosecution. Same-sex conduct carries death by stoning de jure, currently suspended by a moratorium confirmed in 2026 but revocable without warning, plus 7 years/30 strokes or other severe penalties and a secular 20-50 year provision. No border, custody, care or remedy protections are documented, and fear, monitoring and outing threats are reported. Moratorium and sporadic cross-dressing enforcement prevent the 0.05 tier; authorised, revocable execution and direct criminalisation keep it well below 0.25.

entry_documents.exposure: No change of name or gender on official documents and no sex reassignment surgery permitted; a trans visitor cannot align travel documents with presentation. No trans-specific border rule documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/presentation mismatch can trigger the cross-dressing offence and police identification, though border screening practice is not documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Cross-dressing case in 2014-15 resulted in fine and 60 days' imprisonment in default. Custody placement, searches or conditions for trans visitors not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for presentation could escalate investigation under morality/sexual-conduct provisions; no documented consular or bail protection.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Single national religious penal code; no documented subnational variation. Gendered facilities rules for visitors not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: One small territory and one national code mean no local protective regime offsets the national regime.

care_services.exposure: Sex reassignment surgery not permitted in country; visitor access to hormones, prescriptions or emergency care not documented.
care_services.interaction: Disclosure during care could expose the visitor to cross-dressing enforcement; no documented confidentiality protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Section 198(1) criminalises men dressing as women/women as men without reasonable excuse or for immoral purposes. Religious code provides stoning de jure for anal sex/adultery, 7 years/30 strokes where threshold unmet, 40 lashes for sex between women; moratorium revocable at any time.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Death-penalty moratorium extended May 2019, still in effect May 2023 and confirmed 27 Sept 2026; no execution since 1957.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Moratorium mitigates execution only while the monarch does not revoke it; it does not repeal criminalisation or imprisonment exposure.

minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented. No age-specific visitor, schooling or guardianship rule is in the dossier.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police intimidation including threats to make sexuality public to obstruct jobs/graduation; monitoring of activities/communications; discrimination in employment, housing, recreation and services; climate of fear reported 2019.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State-linked outing threats increase consequences of any document or presentation discovery; no documented protective response to anti-trans violence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No assurance new provisions will not be enforced against foreigners; no independent human rights organisations; implementing regulations unissued in 2017; entry/border treatment and remedies for visitors not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Moratorium on executions is the only documented mitigation and is revocable without notice.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of documented remedies cannot be treated as safety, especially where enforcement is sporadic (no known cross-dressing convictions in 2017).

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower severity than 0.05: execution is legally authorised but not recently carried out and is under a confirmed moratorium, whereas 0.05 involves documented lethal custody and a recent execution. Revocability keeps this dossier closer to 0.05 than a no-capital regime.

Similar to 0.15 in direct criminalisation of presentation and capital provision not currently imposed, but higher because dossier documents only a fine/60-day default for cross-dressing and no pattern of beatings, months in pretrial custody, or routine transit arrests.

Lower than 0.25: 0.25 anchors state execution is not imposed/realistic, while here stoning is in force de jure and the moratorium can be revoked without warning, and documents cannot be aligned with presentation.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: one national code criminalises the visitor's presentation itself, documents cannot be changed to match, and sexual-conduct penalties reach death de jure. The operative mitigation is a revocable moratorium, not repeal, plus historically sporadic cross-dressing prosecutions. No documented border, facility, care, custody or legal protections offset exposure, and authorities are documented using outing as intimidation. If outed, a Muslim visitor faces the religious code principally applicable to Muslims; applicability to non-Muslim visitors and exact border practice remain uncertain, but no assurance of non-enforcement against foreigners was given.
